newsitem.title: USA: Stocks rise on gains in technology stocks.
newsitem.headline: Stocks rise on gains in technology stocks.

text.p: Stocks gained ground Tuesday as investors turned their interest to technology, oils and banks.
At 1 p.m. EST, the Dow Jones industrial average was up 10.00 points at 6,928.92.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 14-8 on volume of 310 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The Dow transportation index was up 32.98 points at 2,406.40 helped by a gain in Conrail, which agreed on Monday to negotiate a merger with CSX Corp. for $10.3 billion, or $115 per share. Conrail Inc. rose 1-1/4 to 112-7/8.
The Nasdaq Composite index, a barometer of the high technology shares rallied 12.05 points at 1323.23. The American Stock Exchange index was up 1.84 to 596.66.

"The industry groups which were poor performers in last week's decline are the good performers at the start of this week," said Hugh Johnson, chief investment officer at First Albany Corp. "They are recovering."
He said the cash flow from households into mutual funds continued to be strong and that money managers could only sit on their hands for so long without putting the money into play.

"Money managers are moving into those groups which cheapened up some and have been good relative performers -- the techs, the oils, the banks and some consumer non-cyclicals," Johnson said. "That indicates that a lot of momentum players are returning to these groups."
Among the techs, Intel Corp., the most actively traded Nasdaq issue, was up 2-7/8 at 148-3/4, Cisco Systems Inc. was up 1-3/4 at 56 and Ascend Communications Inc. was up 3-71/6 at 58-1/8.
Dow index component International Business Machines Corp. rose 1-1/8 to 146-1/4.
The blue-chip index also drew strength from the oil stocks. Texaco Inc. was up 1-5/8 at 100-3/8 and Exxon Corp. was up 1-5/8 at 100-3/4. Mobil Corp. was up three at 128-3/8.
BankAmerica Corp. was up 1-5/8 at 116-1/4, Chase Manhattan Corp. gained 7/8 at 102-7/8, Citicorp was up 1-7/8 at 119-1/2.
